text: Thinking about how I used to measure a good day by how much I got done. Lately it's more about whether I was kind.
Ten years since I moved here. Looking back at who I was when I arrived. A lot has changed, some of it on purpose.
Wondering whether I avoid conflict because I'm peaceful or because I'm scared. Probably both.
Read old letters from Gita. We were so certain about everything at twenty. I'm less certain and more at ease now.
Noticing a pattern: every time work gets busy, I stop calling friends. Want to change that.
What would I do if money didn't matter? Same job, I think, fewer hours. That's useful to know.
End of year review. Wins: learned to say no, ran a 5k, stayed in touch with Ade. Misses: still not sleeping enough.
Mum and I talked about her childhood today. Some of my habits make more sense now.
Is ambition something I actually want or something I absorbed? Turning that over all evening.
Funerals make you think. Listening to the speeches for Mr. Ito I wondered what people would say about me.
I'm starting to see that the version of success I chased in my twenties was mostly someone else's.
Long walk, long think. Not sad, not happy, just sorting through things.
The argument with Jonas was about the dishes on the surface. Underneath it's about feeling unseen. Need to say that next time.
I'm the same age Dad was when I was born. Strange to think of him at 34, as unsure as me.
Journaling prompt: what am I tolerating? Answer: a job that drains me, a friendship that's one-sided, my own inner critic.
Sat in the old school car park and remembered being fourteen and so sure everyone hated me. Wish I could tell her it gets better.
Thinking about forgiveness. I don't think I need to forgive Callum to move on. I just need to stop carrying it.
Six months of therapy. Biggest lesson so far: feelings aren't facts.
Watching my parents get older and realising I've started to parent them a bit. Not sure how I feel about it.
What I'd tell my younger self: rest is not laziness. Ask the question. Wear the coat.
Did I move abroad to find something or to escape something? Five years in, I think the answer was escape, and then it became find.
Quiet evening going through photos from the year. More happy moments than I remembered.
Talking with Bilal about faith made me realise mine changed shape rather than disappeared.
I keep saying I want a quieter life and then saying yes to everything. Interesting contradiction.
Wondering what home means now. The house where I grew up is sold. My flat feels temporary. Maybe it's people, not places.
Birthday thoughts at 50: fewer things, more people, better shoes.
Looked at the job description I wrote for myself last year. I've grown into it more than I expected.
I've been thinking about why the comment from Priyanka stung so much. It touched something I already believe about myself.
A year since the diagnosis. I measure time differently now. Before and after.
Spent the evening thinking about what I actually want from a partner, not what looks good on paper.
Mentoring Rhys today, I heard myself give advice I don't follow. Noted.
Pondering the idea that rest is something you plan, not something you earn.
I think the reason I keep busy is that stillness lets the grief in. Writing that down feels important.
Watched the documentary about my hometown and saw it through outsiders' eyes. It's smaller and kinder than I remember.
Every year I write the same goals. Maybe they're not goals. Maybe they're values I already have and just want to notice.
Grandma's diary from 1962 arrived from the attic. She worried about the same things I worry about. Money, love, being enough.
Thinking about how much of my personality is just my mother's anxieties in a nicer outfit.
Conversation with Elena on the train about regret. She says she regrets nothing. I regret a few things and I'm okay with that.
Reviewing the year: hard, important, unexpectedly tender.
I notice I describe my week by what I achieved and never by how I felt. Trying to change the question.
Teaching my daughter to ride a bike, I let go and she went. Thought a lot about letting go after that.
I'm not upset about the promotion going to Shreya. It just made me ask whether I wanted it at all.
Hard to know if I'm growing apart from the old crowd or growing into myself. Same thing maybe.
Spent the morning sorting old notebooks. My handwriting changed when Dad died. I never noticed until today.
What does enough look like? Enough money, enough work, enough approval. Trying to put a number on it.
Talked with Uncle Femi about the war. He spoke for an hour and then said 'that's enough for one day'. Thinking about it still.
First anniversary of moving in with Nico. Learned a lot about compromise. And towels. So many opinions about towels.
Wondering if I quit things too early. Piano, French, the band. Or if I just know when something's not mine.
Noticing how differently I treat myself when I'm sick versus when someone else is sick. Kinder to them.
I keep coming back to something Ms. Adair said in year nine: 'curiosity is a muscle'. Still true.
The breakup taught me that I go quiet when I'm hurt and expect people to guess. Lesson learned, painfully.
Deep thinking day. Who am I when no one needs anything from me? Don't have an answer yet.
Reading about stoicism on the bus. The bit about controlling only your reactions hit home.
Mid-year check-in. Halfway through and I've kept two of five resolutions. The two that mattered most, actually.
Visited the old flat. New family, new paint. I stood across the road and remembered all of it, the good and the awful.
Asked myself why I'm so afraid of being a beginner. I think I learned early that mistakes were dangerous.
Thinking about Ayodele's advice: 'decide who you are, then the decisions get easier'.
Looking at my calendar and asking whose priorities it shows. Not mine.
Something shifted this year. I care less about being liked and more about being honest.
Writing a eulogy for Uncle Pat. Trying to fit seventy-eight years into three minutes. Thinking about what really mattered to him.
Wondering whether to stay in this city or go home. Made a list. The list doesn't help. My gut keeps saying home.
Funny how the worst job I had taught me the most about what I want.
Kieran asked what I'm proud of and I couldn't answer quickly. Thinking about that.
I see now that I was depressed that whole winter. Couldn't name it then. Can name it now.
Considering what I'd keep if the house burned down. Photos, the quilt, the letters. Not much else.
I've realised I'm happiest when I'm making something with my hands. Should probably build my life around that.
Pondering. Nothing in particular. The kind of evening where thoughts wander.
Every relationship I've had, I've been the one to leave first. Worth looking at.
Lunch with Mrs. Oduya, my first boss, retired now. She remembered things about my early career I'd forgotten. Made me see how far I've come.
I think I've confused being needed with being loved for a long time.
